title: Operational stability: staffing & SLO collaboration playbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic, lightweight playbook for staffing, cross-team collaboration, and short-run SLO experiments. It's intended to help feature teams, platform, and SREs coordinate a 30–90 day reliability runway without creating heavy process overhead. Use as template + scratchpad during run planning.

Audience:
SRE leads, platform PMs, product/feature owners, oncall engineers, solutions engineering.

High-level goals:
- Ensure predictable staff coverage for experiments and rollouts tied to SLOs (latency, availability, error-rate).
- Create low-friction cross-functional checkpoints so regressions are caught early.
- Balance staffing cost vs. risk: a simple calculator in Appendix for headcount tradeoffs.

Why this is different from a standard SLO rollout:
- Emphasis on weekly staffing choreography (who is bridging, who is shadowing).
- Short, repeatable experiment cycles (two-week smoke + four-week ramp) instead of single long rollout.
- Explicit knowledge-transfer mini-sprints so product teams carry ops responsibility post-launch.

Core concepts / terms (quick):
- Bridge rotation: a lightweight, short-lived team (1–2 weeks) combining 1 SRE + 1 product engineer + 1 infra/DB owner to handle launch windows.
- Shadow exchange: 3–5 day paired sessions where feature engineers pair with SREs on triage and runbook exercises.
- SLO smoke: short synthetic workloads + canary traffic to validate measurement & alerts.

Roles and responsibilities (template):
- Feature owner (FO): owns SLO definition, alert thresholds (initial proposal), and test plans. FO coordinates customer-impact context and recovery target.
- Service Reliability Lead (SRL): shepherds measurement, alert correctness, and runbook completeness; runs smoke tests.
- Platform/Infra rep: validation of capacity/backpressure and rollout gating for autoscaling rules.
- Release Coordinator (RC): schedules bridge rotations, posts weekly staffing notes, manages oncall swap if needed.

Weekly cadence (suggested):
- Monday 30-min planning: RC + FO + SRL + infra rep. Quick checklist: staffing for the week, outstanding blockers, required canary windows.
- Tuesday morning 60-min smoke window (if any): run synthetic test, validate metrics, note anomalies.
- Wednesday/Thursday shadow exchanges (2–3hrs spread): pairing, runbook rewrite based on smoke outcomes.
- Friday 30-min retro & decision: continue ramp / pause / rollback.

30–90 day runway (example phases):
- Phase 0 (prep, ~2 weeks): define SLO, build measurement dashboards, author runbook draft, schedule shadow exchange.
- Phase 1 (smoke, 1 week): run canary/synthetic tests, fix measurement gaps, update alerts.
- Phase 2 (ramp, 2–4 weeks): progressive traffic increase (10% → 50% → full), staffed bridge rotations at each milestone.
- Phase 3 (operationalize, ongoing): handback to feature team with SRL as steward for 30d, then normal oncall model.

Staffing template (practical):
- Bridge rotation composition: 1 SRL (primary) + 1 Feature engineer (primary) + 1 Infra/backing-service owner (on-call-as-needed).
- Coverage hours: default 9–5 local for primary window; on-call pager remains unchanged except an SRL promotion for escalation 9–11pm during first week of ramp.
- Backup: SRL-2 (backup) assigned from platform pool.

SLO experiment matrix (quick table as bullets):
- Experiment name: Latency tail reduction (model-inference path)
  - Hypothesis: batching + KV caching reduces p99 by >=20% with <5% added CPU utilization.
  - Measurement: p50/p90/p99, token throughput, GPU utilization.
  - Success gate: p99 < 350ms and no >1.5x error rate increase.
- Experiment name: Cache fallout test
  - Hypothesis: cache stampede protection avoids error bursts during eviction.
  - Measurement: error spikes during synthetic eviction cycle.
  - Success gate: no more than 2 bursts >5 minutes across 24h.

Oncall shadow & knowledge transfer checklist (to use during shadow exchange):
- Walk the alert path: source-of-truth query, where metric is computed, and how it surfaces in pager duty.
- Simulate a common failure (e.g., KV missstorm) and follow runbook steps out loud.
- Verify access: logs, dashboards, KMS keys, deploy permissions.
- Backfill docs: one-sentence TL;DR for each runbook step.

Runbook hygiene (minimal viable):
- Problem statement (1–2 lines)
- Quick mitigation (commands or dashboard toggles)
- Root-cause indicators (metrics to inspect)
- Rollback / fallback steps
- Postmortem owner & timeline

Risk heatmap (practical):
- High: single-point-of-failure services (auth, KV). Mitigation: dedicated bridge rotation on launch + immediate rollback gate.
- Medium: non-deterministic load patterns (customer burst). Mitigation: temporary rate-limits, synthetic load tests.
- Low: telemetry gaps; mitigation: short-term additional sampling/tracing for 7d.

Communications & escalation protocol (lightweight):
- Incident begins: SRL posts to #reliability-bridges (channel) and updates RC on staffing needs.
- If SLO breach persists >30 minutes, escalate to platform lead and create JIRA-REL incident ticket.
- Post-incident: 48h postmortem draft by incident owner, circulate to stakeholders within 72h.

Success metrics (KPI candidates):
- Time to detect regression (TTD) baseline vs post-playbook target (goal: <5m for critical alerts).
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for SLO-related incidents (goal: 30–90m depending on severity).
- Fraction of experiments that complete with usable telemetry (target: 80%+).

Milestones (sample 8-week plan):
- Week 0–2: SLO definition, measurement work, assign SRL, recruit bridge roster.
- Week 3: Smoke tests, two shadow exchanges.
- Week 4–6: Ramp windows + two bridge rotations.
- Week 7: Operational handoff + metrics review.

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Who owns the bridge roster long-term? (ops vs product platform?) -> action: product/platform leads to propose roster by 2026-04-15.
- Staffing cost model needs validation against Reserved/Dedicated capacity economics. Jonah to run a 2-week sample.
- Add a small automation to post 'weekly staffing' to #reliability-bridges (low priority).

Appendix: simple staffing calculator (assumptions):
- Bridge rotation = 3 people for 1 week (assume 8 day-equivalent coverage for overlap).
- Cost estimate: SRE rate (fully burdened) = 1.5x engineer rate. Quick calc: 3 engineers * 1 week = 3 engineer-weeks. Multiply by cost rate.

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Keep playbook intentionally lightweight. If this becomes a long-run process it will be ignored.
- Consider adding a 30m monthly 'ops-refinement' to prune runbooks and reduce cognitive overhead.

References / links (operational):
- SLO measurement primer: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELIABILITY/SLO+handbook
- Example PR for telemetry fixes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842

Last updated by Maya Patel (SRL) — feedback welcome.
summary: Lightweight, tactical playbook for staffing bridge rotations, shadow exchanges, and SLO experiment runway to reduce ops overhead and increase early detection. Includes weekly cadence, 30–90 day phases, staffing template, and open action items.
